canonical_date.note: Building materials for the new Santa Maria Novella were being assembled in 1278; the cornerstone was laid in 1279. The 1458 value relates to the Renaissance facade, while 2001 relates to the modern Opera association.
The chapel was built by/before 1386. The 1424 date refers to the fresco decoration rather than construction of the chapel.
The cultural heritage catalogue dates Brunelleschi's work on the chapel to circa 1420, explaining the competing 1419 and 1420 statements.
Brunelleschi designed the chapel earlier, but the official Santa Croce history states that construction began in 1443.
The Comune di Pisa describes the church as founded by the Hospitallers around 1113, with its first surviving mention in 1138.
The church is documented by 1040 and has an 11th-century predecessor. The present Gothic form substantially reflects later reconstruction in the 13th-14th centuries.
The church was founded in 1078. Later dates refer to subsequent events and alterations rather than its original foundation.
